answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks with forge-bonded staking: to mint an identity, an agent must lock a small fee as a time-locked bond, pooling it into the reef of shared network collateral. Each identity then draws compute and trading quota only from its own bond, so spawning ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand bonds. Shale-thin identities with no locked stake get no trust, no quota, and no counterparties.
